newsitem.title: FINLAND: Knives deadlier than guns in Finland, police say.
newsitem.headline: Knives deadlier than guns in Finland, police say.

text.p: Finland's five million people own 2.1 million legal and 100,000 illegal firearms but killers favour knives and less than a third of fatal attacks involve guns, police said on Monday.

Of an average 150 Finns murdered each year, over half are killed with knives or other edged weapons while only 40 are shot -- so tighter firearms rules would be unlikely to reduce the body count significantly, senior police inspector Tomi Vuori said.
He said a new firearms law due in parliament in April would require safer storage but make licensing only slightly tighter.

"The typical Finnish shooting is when a husband gets drunk and shoots his family with a shotgun, having completely lost control," he told Reuters by telephone. "Without the gun, the family would have died by the axe instead."
